svg.title: Reading a vendor offer
svg.desc: 1. Excel: the first sheet is read with SheetJS and known column headings are mapped in code, with no AI. 2. Only when headings are unknown are the first rows sent to the agent, which may only say which column means what; a checker rejects bad mappings. 3. Code moves the values and compares source and result cell by cell; if anything differs, the result is discarded. 4. PDF or Word: the server applies the same guard used for recording a quotation, caps the file at 20 MB and reads the BOQ item names itself. 5. Text is extracted; empty or scanned files are rejected before the agent is called, and the text is cut at 24,000 characters. 6. Every number written in the document is collected into a set; the agent runs one-shot with a 180-second limit and is told never to compute or round. 7. Each returned price must be found in that set or the row is dropped with a reason; totals and specifications are checked the same way. 8. The preview shows source and result side by side with arithmetic and deviation warnings, and nothing is saved until a person presses Save.
